Jabra SPORT Bluetooth Stereo Headset - Black/Yellow (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I am disappointed with these headphones for only one reason: My ears are small, and because of that, these headphones will not snuggly "hang" over my ears like they should. (Children would have the same problem, I expect.) If the over-ear part of the headphones were a little more moldable, I might be able to make them work for me; the extra ear gels themselves are helpful in getting a good fit into the ear canal, but that doesn't keep them from falling off of me. This is why I'm knocking of a star but, again, the problem is not with the headset but with my own anatomy!

With that caveat aside, I love them! For a gardener who wants to listen to something outside while working, the FM radio works just fine and the yellow rubbery cord keeps them around your neck even if you do knock them off. The U.S. Military-grade protection features (against dust, moisture, and shock) make these headphones stand out from the pack.

The Bluetooth pairing and sustained connection with these is better than any other Bluetooth device I've ever used, although I tend not to use Bluetooth unless I'm up and about in the house doing chores. I also don't make or get a lot of phone calls, so we don't even have a cellphone account and depend on the occasional VoIP to get the job done. Meaning I haven't tested the headset features at all.

But the sound is crisp and clear, without mud, more like monitoring headphones used in the music industry. I feel no pressure when wearing them (holding them to my head with my hands, of course, to keep them from falling off of my teensy ears), and I know they would be very comfortable for me in daily use. Maybe I can come up with something to rig them with so they don't fall off. Because I really do like them.
text_fidelity_b: Jabra SPORT Bluetooth Stereo Headset - Black/Yellow (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) - Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 8 GB, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Closeout) Some people have claimed the screen is square, it's not. Like all previous Kindles this is measured diagonally. It only appears square because the one side of the bezel with the buttons (also not loud as has been claimed and the touch screen works fine if the nearly inaudible click might keep a partner awake).
I really like the seven inch screen and design of this new Kindle it's much closer to a regular paperback page now. I do wish the boldness option was allowed to be applied to any book and not just those purchased from Amazon. I get plenty of books from other sites such as Baen and Project Gutenberg but they're not given the full functionality Amazon's books are. I don't think it's fair.
The weight and balance. In or out of the cover is almost perfect. I find I can comfortably read for hours and if either hand gets tired a quick flip and you're reading with the other. I've reversed the page turn buttons like on the old K3/Kindle keyboard the page forward button is more natural feeling if it's at the bottom I have no idea why Amazon has the default reversed. Holding it you're more apt to go forward than bsck plus if you need to go back you can just slide your finger towards the screen and use the touch screen to go back, then it's right back to the lower button to continue reading. I rather like this device. It's noy light years ahead of the Voyage or PaperWhite but it is certainly a few large steps ahead. I haven't and have no plans to test the waterproof claims. I like the idea because I'm disabled and on a walker my previous Kindles have gotten damp. Now i don't have to worry. I did pour a few drops of water on the cover. All but one rolled off. The one soaked in. Caveat emptor. Im happy with the purchase so far. It was a gift to myself for having quit smoking for 10 full years. I deserved it.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Oasis E-reader (Previous Generation - 9th) - Graphite, 7" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi), Waterproof, Built-In Audible, 8 GB, Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers (Closeout)

I wanted an e-ink reader, so I got this when it was offered to me as a discount.

In general, it's okay. I do not read in the dark and try not to use the backlight, but without the backlight the text is pretty dark. I have to use a bold font to read properly. The touch screen is very uncooperative compared with the tablet. You have to poke and poke to get things to work, even turning the pages. I wish there was a volume control on this one which you could use to turn pages instead. It's also not very intuitive where everything is. For instance, once I finish a book and wish to go back to the front to collect information for a review--the copyright date, for instance, or the name of a character--I have to mess around trying to get back to the first page.

I gave it four stars because the battery life is incredible and it doesn't bother my eyes as much, but for the touch screen it might get closer to three stars.

Fire TV Stick 4K streaming device with Alexa Voice Remote (includes TV controls) | Dolby Vision I have the original Fire box, the V2 Fire box and the version of the Fire Stick that came out right before this one. All have performed just fine, but this new stick has some major improvements that I really like.

Setup was as easy as with other Fire devices -- it walks you through the steps on screen. It also does a setup for having the remote control the TV and the receiver (my Fire Stick is plugged into my AV receiver). It works great -- I can power on/off both the TV (Samsung) and receiver (Onkyo) by just pressing the power button on the Fire remote. During power-up it also sets the receiver to the correct port for using the Fire stick. The volume on the remote controls the volume on the receiver. Very handy feature that works every time.

The overall speed and responsiveness is improved over earlier Fire sticks. Menus are more snappy and apps load faster. There are also a number of new settings to control audio and video aspects. I left most on their default, but it's nice to be able to get into the settings and tweak them.

A very nice upgrade to the Fire line. 100% satisfied with the purchase!

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk Sansa Fuze 4 GB Video MP3 Player (Black) This is my daughter's third MP3 player.
She wanted to try this one, since she loved the look of the design.
We figured how bad can a player be, right?
After seeing hers, my son ordered the same player.

Well, they do play music - for a while.
They also play videos nicely, albeit very small and hard to see.

As of today, with neither one a year old yet, one has had be to be sent back
to Sansa for work (totally locked up and could not even be rebooted). They took a
month to send back a refurb, rather than the one my son sent in with his music on it.

My daughter's lasted a little longer, but does freeze up often.
However, the latest trick is that it has part of the sound going out.
She had purchased four pairs of various headphones trying to get the sound to stop
cutting out, thinking it was the headphone's problem. Nope - turns out, it is the
player. Don't know what is wrong, but one of the stereo sides cuts in and out endlessly.

She'll be shopping for a new one, but it won't be this model anymore.
They are just too cheaply made to last. The technology has been around for a long time now,
and it shouldn't be that hard to make a decent, affordable player.
However, it seems like it might just be too hard for Sansa.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk Sansa Fuze 4 GB Video MP3 Player (Black)

LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports A good laptop chiller pad becomes important when you run a lot of graphics-intensive games or if you are doing anything requiring the CPU to run a heavy load. Heat is the enemy of a computer system and the fastest way to a dead laptop is to not deal with heat issues when there’s a problem. I had a chill pad some time ago and it was sub-par. This one by LotFancy is much better and it does a good job.

First off, this is a big chill pad, the same basic dimensions as my laptop but much thicker. I have a 15.6" laptop and this pad is almost a perfect and exact fit, with only a narrow area in the back that extends past the end of the laptop. If you want a small and petite chill pad, this is not the one you want. It does incline too with a metal bar and slots in the case so that the laptop can be angled up. This actually is good for exposing it to even more air.

This chill pad connects to a USB port so it can either be plugged into a port on the computer or into a hub. There are two ports on it and both seem to be the same in terms of how the pad operates. That is, the pad operates at the same speed regardless of which port is used. There are also two buttons on the pad for turning it on. One turns on the larger fan in the middle, and the other turns on all the other fans. Two green LEDs next to those buttons indicate that the pad is powered on and working.

This pad moves a lot of air and it does a good job of cooling the laptop. But, it does so very quietly which is a huge plus. I have it set up in my home office and the pad makes about as much noise as a desktop computer, maybe a little less. The sound it makes is a gentle hum.

When powered on each fan has a bright blue LED in it. While they look cool when there’s no laptop on the pad, they’re all but invisible when the laptop is sitting on top. There isn’t even much of a glow coming from the pad. I turned on the pad, turned out all of the lights and the glow from the laptop screen was enough to overpower any light that might have come from the pad. Except for the low hum I wouldn’t know it was even turned on.

This is a good chill pad. It works quietly and it moves a lot of air. Compared to other chill pads I have used this one is very good and I am happy to recommend it.

Disclaimer: I was provided a sample of this product in exchange for a fair, honest and thorough review. Even though I received this product at no cost I have rated and reviewed this product without bias, based solely on my experience with it.
text_fidelity_b: LotFancy Laptop Cooler Cooling Pad with 5 Quiet Fans for 12-17" Notebook, Dual USB Ports

text_fidelity_a:
MSI G Series GT70 0ND-219US 17.3-Inch Laptop (Black) PROS: Awesome as advertised! Specs and possibly even the parts blow away most high(er)-end laptops in its class...can't beat it for the price. Was debating this over the Samsung Series 7 Gamer with similar specs and both had similar reviews but MSI performed where it counted the most. Better battery, better cooling, mostly better benchmark tests. A big deciding factor for me was that the older MSI GT70 with GTX660/670 still outperformed and outfeatured the Samsung Series 7 Gamer in most of the benchmarking tests...and this next upgrade to MSI GT70 was only $1850 when I bought it...$30 more that the Samsung at the time.

CONS: My only down was with GPU drivers not the actual laptop itself. I think the drivers are so new not even the supposed "BETA" drivers will work with it. It was almost impossible to find the GTX 675m drivers. NVIDIA recommended I get the drivers from the manufacturer's site. And from what I've found there is only one that works and it is on MSI's website. For some reason when I first looked, MSI, didn't have a "notebook" category in their drivers section. It's not even on NVIDIA's site (this had nothing to do with NVIDIA's forums going down, I checked before there forums got hacked).
My reason for purchase.....
First off, I wanted to get this off my chest because I was planning to build a workstation PC (or a powerful PC) but instead switched to getting a laptop. Being that I'm not a laptop fan, I did extensive weeks of research to find the best laptop I could find for my 3d art/animation and gaming needs. Laptop have always been way overpriced and notebook parts can't even touch the PC counterpart; in terms of performance, cooling, etc. Plus, knowing that this an MSI, helped make my decision because they have a good track record of excellent PC parts. I have been building my own desktop PC's for over 10 years and know you get to enjoy the games and 3d applications the way it was meant to be. Also, I'm in the video game development field and needed a second/backup computer/desktop replacement. My current Intel Q9550/Radeon 5700 1GB/ 8GB DDR2 RAM desktop does the JOB but is getting ancient. I was really thinking about getting a workstation or high-end gaming desktop (which would obviously be way cheaper than the most expensive laptop) but after thinking about it, I liked the idea of having the convenience and portability. And, if my desktop goes belly up one day (as it has been acting up) my work flow pipeline won't take a hit. I wont have to deal with the inconvenience of being in a HOT room with 1000W powersupply... even with air conditioning.
text_fidelity_b: MSI G Series GT70 0ND-219US 17.3-Inch Laptop (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150)) UPDATE: Six months in, this router has been flawless. AND I've discovered it has its own dynamic DNS support capability. That's a nice feature if you run any sort of server application. So, I continue to be impressed with this product.

---

I will be keeping a close eye on this router, which I just purchased yesterday, because it seems too good to be true. So far, in my 24 hours of usage since purchasing it for $29 at Walmart (sorry, Amazon, I was in a hurry) I have found it to be flexible and powerful in my unusual application, which is remote and requires 100% uptime with occasional bursts of heavy usage. Mine is a factory-fresh rather than refurb unit, incidentally.

I'll admit I had some trouble believing a router this cheap could be as good as this one turned out to be (assuming it stays reliable-- but, the one I bought trumpets a lifetime guarantee on the box). I expected something dumbed-down, with seriously constrained functionality and annoying firmware. (This model's v3 hardware, although Broadcom BCM5356-based, is not compatible with alternative firmware such as DD-WRT due to its problematic NVRAM size.) It's a single-stream design, with an internalized antenna, potentially suggesting performance limitations. And it's from Netgear, which I've frankly not had great luck with before... but it's been years since I've tried one of their products, and the reviews here are generally good. Most of the negative reviews here relate to support experiences, but my networking knowledge-level is expert, so ...what the heck, did I mention it was $29? An easy roll of the dice.

Though my application requires custom configuration, I initially started the unit using its web-based wizard, which you access by connecting your computer (via cable or WiFi) and pointing your browser to 192.168.1.1. With the unit connected to my cable modem, it set itself up quickly and voila, Internet. For most people this would be good enough and the job would be done. Kudos to Netgear for delivering the product with WPA-2 encryption enabled! They provide a SSID and password on a printed label. So, you're good to go. And its default configuration is just fine for most folks' usage.

For my application, however, I needed to cable several devices including a VoIP adaptor (a la [...] and a server with several ports exposed to the Internet. The unit needed to be set to a specific IP address scheme, SSID and password. And a dynamic-DNS utility on the server needed to communicate with my DNS provider. ...To accomplish these and other advanced tasks, the browser-based configurator at 192.168.1.1 has an Advanced tab. Proceeding through the settings is straightforward and similar to other reasonably-configurable routers. The default settings established earlier by the wizard remain intact in the Advanced panes so you are starting from a known-operable configuration. All good.

So I proceeded through each of my customizations, taking care to click the Apply button after modifying any pane. Usually there's a ten-second delay during which the unit sets up the new settings; a few necessitate that the router reboot itself. Everything went smoothly.

So, for $29 I'd replicated an unusual configuration and everything was working. But how well?

Okay so my wife had to take an important international FaceTime call as I was finishing up. So, for a while there the server was downloading some massive updates, two ssh clients were talking to the server, VoIP was in use, six WiFi clients were doing whatever they were doing, a 3G microcell tower was initializing and downloading firmware updates to itself ...and FaceTime was running smoothly with a high frame-rate on her third-gen iPad. A nice acid test!

In particular, I did not feel the need to mess with the unit's default QoS settings... and additional props to Netgear for including QoS in a router this inexpensive!

So far, I'm impressed. It's hard to imagine a better value in a router. I'll update this review if there are any reliability issues, but so far, so good. So excellent, in fact.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR RangeMax Wireless Router (WNR1000-100NAS (G54/N150))

text_fidelity_a:
WindTook leisure backpack for Women College Book Bag Travel Work Daypack Laptop Computer Bag with USB Charging Port Suits 15 Inch Notebook,Cyan I have had the opportunity to test and review many different back / daypacks and have a good understanding of features and the difference between quality packs and those of lesser quality. This is a quality pack - that being said, this is more of a daypack rather than a travel or school backpack.

The outer shell is a heavy duty canvas material that is definitely made to hold up to wear and tear. I love the outer black and grey color scheme.

The outer most pocket has a zippered pocket (5” x 8”) on the very front and unbuttons at the top to access the full size front pocket (9” x 11”).

Both sides of the bag have snap closed pockets which could carry water bottles or umbrellas. In addition the right side has an exterior USB charging port.

The top of the bag has a double zipper closure that is then covered by a heavy canvas flap that snaps in place via snaps located on the front of the bag. This double sealing system is excellent for both security and waterproofing.

The interior of the primary compartment is HUGE. The lid itself has a zippered mesh pocket for storing items you may need easy access too.

When looking down into the primary compartment, on the left you’ll see the USB cable that leads to the exterior charging port on the right exterior of the bag - this is meant to be plugged into a power supply that then can be stored in the first pouch pocket on the upper interior side of this compartment. Following this pouch there are two smaller, pen sized pouches and then another larger one capable of holding a phone. Above these four pouches is a zippered pocket (7” x 9”). The bottom and rear side of this compartment are heavily padded with the rear wall having double storage specifically for a laptop and tablet. There is a Velcro closure strap that holds your electrics securely in place. The laptop storage area is 10” x 17” while the pocket on the front of that area is 8” x 9” - I was able to squeeze my 17” laptop into the laptop sleeve and Velcro it securely in place and feel like it was adequately protected.

In regards to the shoulder straps, they have a breathable material where they rest against your shoulders which help keep it cooler when carrying. The back is padded and I found the bag comfortable to carry when fully loaded. Above the shoulder straps is a vinyl covered handle that is a bit small for this size bag but is attached well.

All of the snaps, seams and zippers are attached very well - craftsmanship is superb.

While I love the exterior color scheme of this bag, in the bag I received the liner is a bright teal color - obviously this is a personal preference, but I believe it would look much more professional in a royal or navy blue.

This is a great bag for carrying as a daypack - such as to the beach or for an overnight trip. Due to it not being able to unzip and open flat for TSA screening I would not advise it for traveling and it lacks the multiple good sized pockets students require in order to keep their books, notebooks and school supplies organized and easy to find.

This is a well constructed bag that looks nice and is made to hold up. I would certainly recommend it for the purposes I mentioned.

text_fidelity_b: WindTook leisure backpack for Women College Book Bag Travel Work Daypack Laptop Computer Bag with USB Charging Port Suits 15 Inch Notebook,Cyan
